compute.reported_as: The total set of variational parameters theta = (M_mu i, theta_BF, theta_J) are all optimized simultaneously using Variational Monte Carlo and Stochastic Reconfiguration [84]. To accelerate the optimization convergence of our Neural Slater-Backflow-Jastrow ansatz, we initialize the orbital parameters with converged parameters of a Hartree-Fock optimization. For smaller systems (i.e. L = 4) we use shallow backflow CNN networks with one hidden layer and 32 features. For larger and more challenging systems such as L = 8, 10 we construct a residual CNN with 5 convolutional layers and 16 features per filter. [...] To access low-lying energy states, we use the latter residual CNN architecture regardless of the system size. Our deep CNNs use complex-valued weights for the feature maps. [...] We optimize multiple CNN backflow transformation models in parallel, corresponding to the N_f orbitals, ensuring efficient and scalable processing. For the optimization, we use a learning rate of 0.0075. The optimization is carried out using the SR preconditioner with a diagonal shift of 0.001, and we use 4096 Monte Carlo samples.
compute.source: Supplementary Note I (Numerical details and backflow architecture), arXiv:2406.09077 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: One blanket statement for the whole paper: 4096 MC samples. This row is the non-backflow Slater-Jastrow ansatz, so the CNN backflow spec does not apply; its parameters are the Jastrow W_{d(ij)} plus the N_f x N_s orbital matrix (no count given). No hardware, wall-clock or iteration count in the paper.
